speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. The connection to an insect bite and your history of Crohn's disease is important. Has the lesion remained localized to the bite site, and have you noticed any similar lesions elsewhere on your body or any joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of Crohn's disease, anterior uveitis, and the specific morphology of the lesion with purplish borders strongly suggest Erythema Nodosum or Pyoderma Gangrenosum, but we must rule out venous stasis complications. Let me examine the lesion directly to assess for pathergy and check if there are any signs of active infection or systemic involvement. REQUEST TEST: Wound Culture and Biopsy of lesion edge
